content: 1. The metabolism of flibanserin via the intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 is significantly affected by moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, making their coadministration contraindicated. This interaction can lead to severe hypotension or syncope. For example, voriconazole increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and its use with flibanserin is contraindicated. 2. Zileuton also increases flibanserin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and its coadministration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe adverse effects such as hypotension or syncope. 3. Amobarbital decreases flibanserin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug in such cases. 4. Apalutamide decreases flibanserin levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism. Coadministration with strong CYP2C19 inducers like apalutamide can reduce the therapeutic effect of CYP2C19 substrates. Avoid or substitute another drug when possible, and monitor for loss of therapeutic efficacy if coadministration is unavoidable. 5. Flibanserin increases colchicine levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) inhibition. Avoid coadministration with colchicine, especially in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. If necessary, reduce the colchicine dose or frequency as per prescribing information. 6. Eslcarbazepine acetate decreases flibanserin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as strong CYP3A4 inducers substantially reduce flibanserin systemic exposure. 7. Fexinidazole increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as coadministration may increase the risk of adverse effects associated with CYP3A4 substrates. 8. Ivosidenib decreases flibanserin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates or replace them with alternative therapies. If unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic efficacy. 9. Lonafarnib increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for adverse reactions and reduce the dose of CYP2C19 substrates as per product labeling. 10. Lorlatinib decreases flibanserin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as coadministration may reduce flibanserin efficacy. 11. Flibanserin and metoclopramide intranasal both increase each other's effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug, depending on the clinical importance of the drug to the patient. 12. Flibanserin and olopatadine intranasal both increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as coadministration increases the risk of CNS depression, leading to additive psychomotor impairment and daytime dysfunction. 13. Ozanimod increases flibanserin toxicity through adrenergic effects, including elevated blood pressure and heart rate. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Monitor for hypertension if coadministration is necessary. 14. Flibanserin increases repotrectinib levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Ribociclib increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. 16. Flibanserin increases rimegepant levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Flibanserin and ropeginterferon alfa-2b both increase neuropsychiatric side effects. Avoid use and monitor for excessive CNS toxicity. 18. Tucatinib increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with CYP3A substrates, as even minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose as per product labeling. 19. Flibanserin increases venetoclax levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If a P-gp inhibitor must be used, reduce the venetoclax dose by at least 50% and monitor closely for signs of venetoclax toxicity. 20. Flibanserin and zuranolone both increase CNS depressant effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, consider dose reduction. 21. Acetaminophen increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for increased adverse effects, especially when coadministered with multiple weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. 22. Acetaminophen IV and rectal formulations also increase flibanserin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 23. Acrivastine and flibanserin both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 24. Alprazolam and flibanserin both increase sedation. Modify therapy and monitor closely, as the risk of sedation increases with coadministration of CNS depressants. 25. Amisulpride and flibanserin both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 26. Amlodipine increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for increased adverse effects. 27. Amobarbital and flibanserin both increase sedation. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 28. Aripiprazole and flibanserin may interact through serotonin modulation, potentially increasing the risk of neuroleptic malignant syndrome or serotonin syndrome. Use caution and monitor for signs of toxicity. 29. Armodafinil increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 30. Asenapine and flibanserin may interact through serotonin modulation, increasing the risk of neuroleptic malignant syndrome or serotonin syndrome. Both drugs also increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 31. Atorvastatin increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 32. Avapritinib and flibanserin both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 33. Azelastine increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 34. Belzutifan decreases flibanserin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. If coadministration is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates as per prescribing information. 35. Benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen and flibanserin both increase serotonin levels, potentially leading to serotonin syndrome. They also increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 36. Flibanserin increases berotralstat levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor. 37. Betamethasone increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 38. Flibanserin increases betrixaban levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Decrease the betrixaban dose to 80 mg once, then 40 mg daily if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. 39. Bortezomib increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 40. Bosentan decreases flibanserin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor, as strong CYP3A4 inducers substantially reduce flibanserin systemic exposure. 41. Brexanolone and flibanserin both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 42. Brexpiprazole and flibanserin both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 43. Brimonidine and flibanserin both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 44. Brivaracetam and flibanserin both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 45. Bromocriptine increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 46. Brompheniramine and flibanserin both increase sedation. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 47. Buprenorphine and flibanserin both increase sedation. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 48. Buprenorphine buccal, subdermal implant, transdermal, and long-acting injection formulations all increase sedation when coadministered with flibanserin. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 49. Butabarbital and flibanserin both increase sedation. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 50. Butalbital and flibanserin both increase sedation. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 51. Butorphanol and flibanserin both increase sedation. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 52. Cannabidiol increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider reducing the dose of sensitive CYP2C19 substrates when coadministered with cannabidiol. 53. Carbamazepine decreases flibanserin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor, as strong CYP3A4 inducers substantially reduce flibanserin systemic exposure. 54. Carbinoxamine and flibanserin both increase sedation. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 55. Cariprazine and flibanserin may interact through serotonin modulation, increasing the risk of neuroleptic malignant syndrome or serotonin syndrome. Both drugs also increase sedation. Use caution and monitor. 56. Cenobamate decreases flibanserin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism and increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Consider dose reduction of CYP2C19 substrates when coadministered with cenobamate. 57. Chloral hydrate and flibanserin both increase sedation. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
